findings.claim: All shaping processes pour or inject liquid or semi-liquid material into a mould cavity.
findings.truth: R014 includes powder metallurgy for ceramic products as a shaping process; it compacts and sinters powder rather than filling a mould cavity as a liquid.

findings.claim: Wasting-process swarf and offcuts cannot be recovered.
findings.truth: Swarf and offcuts are not part of the component, but suitable scrap can be collected and recycled.

findings.claim: A one-word process type scores only 1 mark and a mechanism scores full marks.
findings.truth: R014 uses a range of question types; the specification sets no universal mark allocation for an explain response.

findings.claim: Two flashcard prompts name the OCR R041 specification.
findings.truth: This unit is R014: Principles of engineering manufacture.

findings.claim: Powder metallurgy is taught for ceramic or metal powders and self-lubricating bearings.
findings.truth: The R014 shaping-process content limits this item to powder metallurgy for ceramic products.

findings.claim: A knowledge-check prompt identifies the OCR R041 specification.
findings.truth: The relevant assessed unit is R014.
Ferrous materials contain iron, but magnetism depends on the alloy; austenitic stainless steels can be non-magnetic or only weakly magnetic.
findings.evidence: British Stainless Steel Association, Is stainless steel non-magnetic? (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.truth: Alloys are metallic mixtures and can contain more than one phase.
findings.evidence: International Union of Crystallography, The study of metals and alloys by X-ray powder diffraction methods (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: A flashcard prompt names the OCR R041 specification.
findings.truth: The relevant assessed unit is R014.

findings.claim: Two flashcard prompts identify their content as OCR R041.
findings.truth: The relevant assessed unit is R014.

findings.claim: Continuous production is presented as an alternative named R014 scale of manufacture.
findings.truth: R014 names one-off, batch and mass manufacture; continuous is not one of its listed scale terms.

findings.claim: CAM removes human error during cutting.
findings.truth: The specification supports improved consistency and reduced defects, not elimination of human error.

findings.claim: Minimum acceptable dimension equals nominal minus lower deviation.
findings.truth: A stated lower deviation is signed, so the minimum dimension is nominal plus that lower deviation; a negative lower deviation has the effect of subtraction.

findings.claim: The stated go/no-go direction applies to every feature.
findings.truth: The stated plug-gauge test applies to holes; shafts use ring or snap gauges with the appropriate limits.
findings.evidence: MSC Industrial Supply, Go/No-Go Gauge Information Guide (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Grinding composite materials produces carcinogenic fibres.
findings.truth: Grinding can generate hazardous fine dust, but carbon fibres are not established as carcinogenic; their principal handling hazard is mechanical irritation.
findings.evidence: OSHA Technical Manual, Section III, Chapter 1 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: The UK Modern Slavery Act means companies can be held accountable for all employment conditions throughout their supply chains.
findings.truth: For qualifying UK organisations, section 54 requires an annual modern-slavery statement about steps taken; it does not require a guarantee that every supply chain is slavery-free or regulate all wages and conditions.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Publish an annual modern slavery statement (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: The specification covers five material-selection criteria and R014 exams directly assess choosing materials by properties.
findings.truth: R014 covers material properties, forms of supply and applications, but its assessment guidance says students are not expected to suggest materials for applications from their properties. Either reframe the whole lesson as non-exam enrichment or move it; a local correction would leave its content, questions and tips mis-scoped.
findings.evidence: J823 section 4.2, Topic Area 2.3 and Assessment guidance

findings.claim: R014 exam preparation includes specified inspection instruments and their precision values.
findings.truth: R014 assesses drawing conventions and tolerance calculations. Its guidance does not require instrument selection; named measuring instruments belong to the R015 practical unit, while feeler and go/no-go gauges are not listed there. Rehome or explicitly mark this block as enrichment rather than making a partial edit.
findings.evidence: J823 sections 4.2 R014 Topic Area 3.1 and 4.3 R015 Topic Area 2

findings.claim: The R014 exam assesses the five-step risk-assessment process and its hierarchy of controls.
findings.truth: R014 asks for safety measures for its named processes. Risk assessment — hazards, risks and control measures — is specified in R015, while this lesson also introduces unrelated processes such as manual arc welding and composite grinding. Reframe or move the lesson rather than performing piecemeal edits.
findings.evidence: J823 sections 4.2 R014 Topic Area 1.2 and 4.3 R015 Topic Area 1.3

summary: Sixteen verified surgical fixes are supplied. Three wider scope problems require editorial adjudication rather than local edits.
